findings.passage: Voting is a fundamental right of our constitution, and I will never stop fighting to protect it for every eligible voter. As your State Representative, I will put my experience in leading teams and building technology to protect our voting rights and ensure that every eligible voter has access to the ballot box. It’s time for free, fair and transparent voting for all eligible voters in Georgia.
findings.note: Campaign issues page, undated. States a general commitment to voting access for eligible voters. Does not mention photo ID or proof of citizenship.

findings.passage: Voting rights…My platform is about affirming the rights of Georgians and proactively working to build unity, inclusivity and opportunity. I would apply that also to voting. How we, at the local level, at the state level, are working to expand all eligible voters’ opportunities to cast a vote and do it with convenience, ease and security.
findings.note: Quoted in a Cobb County Courier candidate interview. The article also says she supports secure drop boxes, voting by mail and same-day registration (article text, not her quote).

findings.passage: Try to go to the various county websites or the secretary of state website to download your absentee ballot these days. It’s not straightforward. It’s not easy.
findings.note: Quoted in the same Cobb County Courier interview, about how hard it is to get an absentee ballot. Does not mention ID.

findings.passage: For too long, the gun issue has been discussed in public forums almost exclusively as a right for citizens to bear arms.  But what about the right of all Georgians to live a life free from the constant fear of being shot in our own house, backyard or school? The people of GA House District 35 are ready for responsible gun violence prevention laws and practices.
findings.note: Campaign-site Ending Gun Violence section; undated page. She says Georgians are ready for gun violence prevention laws.

findings.passage: Death due to gun violence is preventable and all studies show that gun safety measures, laws and practices are proven to reduce injury and death.  Evidence overwhelmingly suggests that the removal of concealed carry permitting systems is associated with higher rates of gun homicide and violent crime.
findings.note: Campaign-site statement on gun safety measures and on removing carry permit systems.
subjects: carry a gun without a permit

findings.passage: To drive down gun deaths, Surgeon General Murthy calls on the U.S. to ban assault weapons and large-capacity magazines for civilian use, introduce universal background checks for purchasing guns, regulate the industry, pass laws that would restrict their use in public spaces and penalize people who fail to safely store their weapons.
findings.note: Campaign-site text reporting the Surgeon General's call for these measures, in the section where she lists the gun bills she supported. Not framed as her own proposal in this sentence.

findings.passage: As your GA State House Representative, I supported key changes and legislation to address this urgent public health crisis, reduce gun violence, save lives, and promote public safety in Georgia:
findings.note: Lead-in to her campaign-site list of gun bills she says she supported: HB44 universal background checks, HB161 safe storage, HB195 firearms safety course, HB224 report lost or stolen guns, HB553 risk protection orders, HB554 semiautomatic assault weapon to a minor, HB555 rapid-fire modifications, HB584 red flag law.

findings.passage: Enact evidence-based laws that are are overwhelmingly supported by Georgians, and proven to reduce the risk of gun violence such as restraining orders for domestic abusers and background checks to keep guns out of the hands of those who have a history of hospitalization for mental illness including:
findings.note: Campaign-site policy line: restraining orders for domestic abusers and background checks tied to mental-illness hospitalization.
